findings.location: definitions enforcementDigests.rbacClosureDigest.refusals ('rbac: malformed input'); README 5.2's new clause; vectors (none for this route)
findings.finding: C2-3's text addition is in place, and the model does produce it on the closure route. Probed: clusterRoles = "x", roles deleted, and roleBindings = {} on the unit snapshot each give 'rbac: malformed input' for rbacClosureDigest. No vector pins this route, though. The text occurs only in MI-01, for the rbac projection, reached through the qualification-namespace check. So a port or model that reports malformed RBAC lists on the closure as 'rbacClosureDigest: malformed input' still passes everything. Probed: a WORK mutant that re-raises the closure's 'rbac: malformed input' as 'rbacClosureDigest: malformed input' survives all 320 checks. The impact is text-level only: the value refuses either way, and VPO's external text is unchanged. R-C2 (a) admitted text additions only for C2-3, so a vector here would have been outside candidate 3. Candidate 3 is correct not to add one.

findings.finding: The brief allows build_contract.py to differ 'only where it pins its sources' digests or names the candidate'. Besides those changes, the build's diff adds the two ruled vectors' definitions and a verbatim-quote check of the R-C2 (a) line. I judge both to follow from R-C2 (a). vectors.json is generated by this script, so G-22b and RB-32 cannot exist without their V() definitions. The R-C2 quote uses the build's existing decisions-pinning mechanism, the same way candidate 2 quoted R-C1-9: the line must occur exactly once, inside its dated section, in the pinned file. It changes no output byte. Neither touches the git helper, the fixtures or any other vector. They are recorded here only because the brief asks to name every change outside its literal list.

checks.check: G-22b against C2-1's requiredChange (brief item 3)
checks.result: Matches. Its ops equal G-22's except the answer's wallMs, which is 40 s earlier: {monotonicMs 700000, wallMs = completed set's startedWallMs + 60000}. The sets are (600000, completed) and (660000, incomplete). The monotonic age from the completed set's own start is 100000 ms, over the 90000 ms bound; the wall age is 60000 ms, inside it. The age from the newest entry would be 40000 ms. Expect and model agree: 'capture set too old' for mutationBroker, networkEnforcementDigest and hostPreflightDigest.

checks.check: RB-32 against C2-2's requiredChange (brief item 3)
checks.result: Matches. RoleBinding 'a' is in the qualification namespace (unit-namespace) with roleRef ClusterRole 'missing-role' (absent from the unit ClusterRoles). ClusterRoleBinding 'b' has roleRef 'unit-viewer' (present) and subject kind Robot. The model gives 'rbac: malformed subject kind' for rbac and rbacClosureDigest. With 'a' alone the result is 'rbac: role does not exist'; with 'b' alone, 'rbac: malformed subject kind'. So the binding order decides the text.
